report.math_notes:
Target: U(Q_5) exactly + optimal labelling in required format. Both directions checked.

UPPER BOUND 88: labelling verified by hand. R={00000,11110} at distance 4, so their neighbourhoods are disjoint; the 6 odd vertices not adjacent to R are exactly the weight-3 words ending in 1 (11001,10101,01101,10011,01011,00111); P = 14 even vertices (10 of weight 2, 4 of weight 4 other than 11110), all distinct, 32 strings form a bijection. Labels 1-8 are valleys (all neighbours higher), leaves 9-18 have exactly one lower neighbour (their star centre) so p=1, each peak has 5 lower neighbours all with p=1 so p=5; T = 18 + 70 = 88. Also consistent with Lemma 3 (v=8, X=0) and Lemma 7 (4*14 = 48+8).

LOWER BOUND 88: Lemmas 1-7 checked line by line and correct (Lemma 2 p>=max(1,deg^-); Lemma 3 T=80+v+X exact; Lemma 4 acyclicity via max-label vertex on a cycle; Lemma 5 bounds c(u) with i=1 forcing a heavy in-neighbour; Lemma 7 in-degree sum 5q+s_H+(32-q-|H|-v)=80 valid because every non-peak non-heavy vertex has p=1 hence deg^- in {0,1}). Case analysis for T<=87 (X<=6, |H|<=2): |H|=2 killed by 4q in {47,45,43}; |H|=0 forces v=4,q=13; |H|=1 forces all in-neighbours of u light, i in {2,3,4}, q=12, and all out-neighbours of u are peaks. Reduction to (*) (independent 12-set I, vertex u not in I, Q_5-(I∪{u}) a forest) is correct, including the passage from |I|=13 to |I|=12.

Finite verification of (*): I have no execution tool and trusted_observations is empty, so the reported outputs (1377 / 3672 sets, 0 acyclic complements) are not independently observed. However (a) both scripts were read and are correct exhaustive exact decision procedures (backtracking with valid remaining-count bound; forest test edges = vertices - components; union-find alternative; XOR-translation symmetry reduction is sound and 3672*12/32=1377 is consistent), and (b) I re-derived the refutation of (*) by hand: using Q_5 = Q_4 x K_2 and the Q_4 one-class neighbourhood function f(s) = 0,4,6,7,7,8,8,8,8, one gets |N(A)| >= |A|+5 for every set A of 2..10 even vertices, so an independent 12-set is either contained in one parity class or is {a} ∪ (11 odd non-neighbours of a) (and its parity mirror). Single-class case: 4 remaining even vertices contain two distance-2 pairs whose 4-cycles (through shared odd neighbours) cannot all be broken by removing one vertex u (adjacent pairs sharing an index leave a 6-cycle when u is the common odd neighbour; disjoint pairs use disjoint odd pairs); 3 remaining even vertices always contain a distance-2 pair since A(5,4)=2. Mixed case: the complement contains a subdivided K_5 (branch vertices N(a), subdivision vertices at distance 2 from a), which stays cyclic after deleting any vertex. Hence (*) fails, so every labelling has T>=88, matching the construction. U(Q_5)=88=|E|+8. Random sampling and annealing (code_6, code_7) are evidence only and were not used.

limitation: No code execution available; the computational outputs of code_2/code_3 are reported by the submitter, not observed by me. The verdict does not depend on them: the code was reviewed for correctness and the finite claim (*) was independently refuted by a hand argument recorded in math_notes.
